newsitem.title: ECUADOR: IMF sees Ecuador 1998 inflation at 15 pct - gov't.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Ecuador 1998 inflation at 15 pct - gov't.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund expects Ecuador's annual inflation rate to fall to 15 percent by the end of 1998, an Ecuadorean official said Friday.
"The IMF is convinced that our inflation next year will be 15 percent," Danilo Carrera, head of Ecuador's policy-setting Monetary Board, told reporters.
That differs with the government's forecast of inflation of between 20 and 22 percent next year. For 1997, the government has forecast inflation of between 28 and 30 percent.
Carrera indicated that inflation could decline next year if the fiscal situation improved.

Separately, Fidel Jaramillo, the central bank's general manager, linked higher-than-expected inflation in July to "El Nino" -- the periodic climatic phenomenon that warms up the waters of the eastern Pacific Ocean. Meteorologists have identified the build-up of a strong Nino this year.
Jaramillo said the weather changes caused by El Nino led to heavy rains and landslides last month, which damaged agricultural crops, mainly rice and sugar.
That was partly responsible for a rise in monthly inflation to 2.06 percent, higher than the 1.9 percent forecast by the Central Bank.
"We are expecting that in coming months, inflation will fall to average levels of below two percent. Either way the variation in July is tolerable," Jaramillo said.
Ecuador's accumulated inflation in the first seven months of the year came to 19.8 percent.
((--Franz Bastidas, Quito Newsroom, 5932 258429 x 113 e- mail: reuters1@reutersecu.com.ec))
